messages:
alex: FYI a handful of east-1b GPU nodes failed MIG enable after last night's driver rollout (535.54 -> 535.60). Seeing profiles disappear and device UUIDs remapped.

sara: which nodes?

alex: gpu-az1b-02, gpu-az1b-07, gpu-az1b-11

kai: logs?

alex: paste: ```
Mar 18 03:12:22 gpu-az1b-02 nvidia-mig-manager[1234]: reconcile failed: UUID mismatch expected 3ee2c1a9-.... got 8b9f2d44-....
Mar 18 03:12:23 gpu-az1b-02 kernel: nvidia: mig-profile apply error: profile not found for device uuid 8b9f2d44-....
```

alex: nvidia-smi shows no MIG profiles on those devices

ben: also seeing NCCL kernel warnings in pods pinned to those GPUs, connecting fails with 'transport endpoint not connected'

sara: could be kernel module mismatch vs driver, we bumped kernels in that batch too

kai: tried restarting nvidia-mig-manager? any effect?

alex: restart did nothing, but clearing /var/lib/nvidia/mig-cache and restarting caused manager to re-detect correct mapping on one node (gpu-az1b-02) but others still fail

oncall: taking ownership, will cordon and try reprovisioning MIG profiles via orchestration

deploy-bot: Scheduled node reboot for gpu-az1b-07 at 04:10 UTC by @oncall

alex: note: something odd — after clearing cache, the kernel assigned new device node numbers (nvidia0 -> nvidia2) which broke our device-plugin symlink expectations

sara: can we re-run device plugin daemonset to recreate symlinks? That could transiently restore pods

alex: tried, device-plugin recreated but kubernetes still sees empty allocatable GPUs on two nodes

kai: I suspect driver update changed nvml UUID stable mapping; the MIG profile metadata in orchestration is keyed by old UUIDs -> reconciliation fails

ben: quick mitigation: fallback to using generic whole-GPU allocation for affected nodepool until we can reconcile MIG mapping

oncall: doing that now: changing nodepool config to disable MIG scheduling for east-1b-legacy for 2 hours

sara: configuration note: when we rolled drivers we skipped the nv-hostkernel package on those hosts due to a packaging issue — that might explain kernel mismatch

alex: AHA; nv-hostkernel absent -> different kernel module loaded -> UUID mapping shifts. Opening a runbook entry

kai: plan: 1) cordon nodes 2) reboot with nv-hostkernel installed 3) clear mig cache 4) run mig-config apply --force 5) uncordon

oncall: ETA 90m for remediation window, posting to #incidents and customers

sara: also adding a detection alert: if mig-manager reports 'UUID mismatch' emit page

ben: noted cost/ops question: if we drain and reprovision, we'll be temporarily down 3 GPUs ~24h of work hours -> minor capacity hit, will affect throughput for a couple of teams

alex: will follow up with postmortem with root cause: driver packaging gap + stale mig-cache + orchestration relying on UUIDs

sara: thx, keep thread updated :thumbsup:
